code-appearance.text:
What the code needs for these boards:
- Order Theme (System, Light, Dark), then Tone, then Accent. Today both apps show Mode (System, Light, Dark), Accent color, Background tone (AppearanceSection.kt:82-91, AppearanceControls.swift:15-59). bae change.
- “Tone” and “Accent” in every locale. Today “Accent color” and “Background tone” (strings.xml:235-236, AppearanceControls.swift:21, :59). bae change.
- The Accent row names the chosen colour on its second line, in secondary, as Theme and Tone show theirs: “Pink” (Android: the CardRow subtitle under “Accent”, from accent.label; macOS: under the Accent label, from accent.title). Both names exist already as the swatches' accessibility labels.

code-casting.text:
What the code needs for these boards:
- While casting is on, the Casting page lists the receivers bae finds with the picker’s own rows (tap to cast; the one being cast to says Casting), from the same device-local table the picker reads, and browses only while the page is open, as the picker does. spec/bae.md §7 “Finding receivers” says devices are searched for only while the picker is open; it changes to the picker or this page. Today the page has no list (CastingSettingsTab.swift, SettingsCastSection.kt). bae change.
- Until the first receiver answers, the list shows a spinner and “Looking for receivers…” (MacSpinner, AndroidSpinner); it fills in as receivers answer, with no end state, since browsing runs while the page is open.
- Convert to shows while casting is on, as today (CastTranscodeFormatPicker).
- Turning casting off while a cast plays asks “Turn off casting?” / “This will stop casting to <device>.” as today; not drawn.
- Android: the switch's explanation is a caption under the card, not the row's second line, which cut it off.
- The page's rows end in ⋮ (Android) or a ⋯ button (macOS) in place of Disconnect, as Welcome's library rows do: Details… on every row, and Disconnect on the one being cast to. The picker keeps Disconnect on its row. spec/bae.md §7 “The Casting page” changes with it. bae change.
- Details: a sheet (Android) or a popover off the ⋯ (macOS) titled with the receiver's name: Type (Chromecast, AirPlay, UPnP), Model, and Address. No status: the row already says Casting. The receiver list carries only id, name and kind today (BridgeCastReceiver); the model comes from what the receiver advertises (a Cast or AirPlay TXT record, a UPnP device description) and the address from where discovery found it (RendererDevice's connection), so both reach the device-local receiver table and the bridge. A receiver that states no model leaves the row out. bae change.

code-history.text:
What the code needs for these boards:
- Listening history offers Off, Only me and Everyone. Today two: Only me and Household (BridgeSharing Private, Household: bae-bridge/src/types/personal.rs:4, mirroring bae-db's people::Sharing; strings.xml:370-371, HistorySharingSection.kt). Off is a third value: bae records no new plays for the person while it is set, and plays recorded before stay as they were (work-history-off). Household reads Everyone in every locale. bae change (bae-db, the bridge, both apps), with spec/bae.md's history section.

code-invite.text:
What the code needs for the invite boards (refs are main as of Nov 6):
- The People list is followed by the invite: on macOS an “Invite…” button under the box, on the right (today “Invite a person…”, MembersSection.swift:100), “Invite” with a + on Android (today a filled “Invite a person” button after the list, MembersScreen.kt:356, strings.xml:347). bae change.
- The form asks only what the storage shares with: their Dropbox, Microsoft or Apple Account email, or on S3 an access key, with a line saying why; on S3, Use my key instead (under the fields on Android, left of the footer on macOS) hands them your own key, saying that removing them later means a new key on each of your devices; then Create invite. No name, no role (everyone joins as Member), no in person or sent, a week to expire. Today: name, role, “Their account email” or keys, In person or Send, an expiry, “Create invitation” (InvitePersonSheet.swift, InviteDialog.kt). coven change (§13.2: the join request carries the name, not the invite; one kind of invite, always approved by comparing the number; confirm §14.3 lets two members share one S3 key), then bae; the spec's walk-through (spec/bae.md:2369) changes with it.
- The invite screen, titled Invite: while sharing, a bar and “Sharing the library with <email>…”; offline, that the code shows once this device is online; then one MacScanCode or AndroidScanCode: what to do, the QR code alone (no code text beside it), Copy code and Share, how long until it expires (“Expires in 7 days”, relative, as InviteCodeSheet.swift does today) and that the request shows up within seconds. The code has no such shared view yet: InviteCodeSheet.swift and InviteShownDialog.kt each lay out the QR code themselves. Today one spinner and “Sharing the library. The code shows once this library syncs.” online or not (InviteCodeSheet.swift:89, strings.xml:401); an in-person invite shows only the QR code, a sent one only the code; the title is the invitee's name. bae change.
- While the invite screen is open, the app asks sync to check every 5 seconds, as Add device does (bae-library/src/manager/people.rs, sync_often). Today nothing does for invites. bae change.
- An open invite's row: its email (its key on S3), Invited, and a chevron that opens its screen; Shares access once online while offline; Joining once approved. No refresh button: today “Check for requests” (MembersSection.swift:448, MembersScreen.kt InviteRow). bae change.
- Their request: “Approve request?”, then “<name> used your invite to <email>”, the number, Decline and Approve. Today the request sheet shows the invitee's name, “Confirmation number” and the number, Close, Decline, Approve (MembersSection.swift JoinRequestSheet). bae change.
- Cancel invite asks first: “Cancel this invite?” with Keep. Today the same confirmation with core's words (core.invite.cancel_confirm.*). Matches; words only.
- S3: the code screen also shows the key's ID and says to delete the key if nobody uses the invite (spec/bae.md:2412). Built (InviteCodeSheet.swift keyLine); not drawn yet.
- A sharing failure a retry can't fix (no such account, say) ends the invite by itself, as a failed request check does (coven spec §13.2). Its row becomes a notice, “Couldn’t invite: Dropbox has no account for it”, with Dismiss; there is no failed screen to cancel from. A failure a retry can fix keeps retrying, the invite still Sharing. Today the invite stays open with coven's held reason, in its row and screen, until it is cancelled (InviteCodeSheet.swift:80, MembersSection.swift InviteRow). coven change (end the invite on a permanent sharing failure, keeping why for the app), then bae.
- Queued: plans/invites.md; coven in todo.md §2 #214 (one kind of invite, the name in the request, a permanent sharing failure ends the invite, two members on one S3 key), bae in #215 after the coven pin bump.

code-library.text:

- Library is five rows, with Sync and People and devices on their own pages. Today both apps show everything inline (LibrarySettingsTab.swift:43-105, SettingsScreen.kt:109-198). bae change.
- macOS: Library folder with Show in Finder replaces the Path row (LibrarySettingsTab.swift:45). bae change.
- Removing the library leaves this page for the welcome list. Today it's here (LibrarySettingsTab.swift:105, SettingsScreen.kt:198). bae change.

code-make-admin.text:
What the code needs for these boards:
- The change box (Changes from this device: Waiting to sync, then Done with Dismiss) shows on the page of the person it changes, above Role. It exists today, with waiting, done, refused, stopped and Dismiss, but on the Library page (AdminChangesSection.swift, shown from LibrarySettingsTab.swift:86) and on Android's people screen (MembersScreen.kt:183, SettingsLibraryModel.kt:121). A rename's change shows on the Library page, under Name. bae change: where it shows, not what it does.

code-name.text:

code-people.text:
What the code needs for these boards (refs are main as of Nov 6):
People and devices
- Two sections, You and People. Under You: a read-only Role row and a Devices row that opens Your devices. Today one People section with a You marker (MembersSection.swift:61, :292). bae change.
- Add device pairs like an invite instead of showing the restore code (plans/add-device-pairing.md; coven todo.md §2 #227, bae #228). The code screen is a MacScanCode or AndroidScanCode: “Scan or enter the code on the new device.”, the QR code alone, Copy code and Share, and “Works while this stays open. Once the new device enters it, its request shows up here within seconds.” The request replaces it in place: “Tablet wants to join. Add it if its screen shows this number.”, the number, Decline and Add. Closing the screen ends the pairing. On S3 only the QR code carries the access key; a device that enters the copied code asks for it. Today the screen shows the restore code as a QR code and text, with the S3 key line (AddDeviceSheet.swift, AddDeviceDialog.kt). coven change, then bae.
- Your devices: each device, this one reading This device with no Remove (it leaves by removing the library from it, ActiveDevice::removable, bae-people/src/membership.rs:91); then adding: on macOS an “Add device…” button under the box, on the right; on Android an “Add device” row with a +, last. bae change.
- Each other person is one row (role, device count) that opens their page: Role with Make admin or Make member, Remove from library in red, their devices. Today macOS lists people with their devices and buttons in one box (MembersSection.swift:63, :326), Android in one list (MembersScreen.kt:437). bae change.
- “Remove from library”. Today Android reads “Remove person” (strings.xml:335) and macOS a trash glyph, “Remove from the library” (MembersSection.swift:313). bae change.
- A member's person rows open nothing. coven lets a member read every person's devices; bae leaves that page out on purpose: a member has nothing to do there.
- Android: Listening history is a choice of AndroidRadio rows in an AndroidDialog; the code has no radio row yet. bae change.
- Android says “this device”, never “this phone”: today “Changes from this phone”, “Saved on this phone” and the recovery-code lines (strings.xml:384-397, :419). bae change, every locale.

code-playback.text:
What the code needs for these boards:
- Countdown belongs to Pause between sides and discs: it sits right under it in the same group, with no divider between them (MacRow and AndroidRow `nested`). Today Android puts it in its own row after the switch (SettingsPlaybackSection.kt:54). bae change, macOS and Android.

code-ratings-playlists.text:
What the code needs for ratings and playlists (no screen yet):
- The bridge reads ratings, playlists and a playlist's entries once (`ratings()`, `playlists()`, `playlist_entries()` in bae-bridge/src/handle/personal.rs), so a screen would miss a change from another device. They become subscriptions, as `subscribe_profiles` is, with the screens that show them.
- spec/bae.md §10.2 (line 3846) already lists them as subscriptions; until then that line is wrong.

code-rename.text:

Today macOS renames from the main menu (MainMenu.swift), Android from a Rename button under the name (SettingsLibrarySection.kt:179). bae change: where it starts.

The list is the one the welcome screen shows (code-welcome). bae change, Android.

code-sync.text:
What the code needs for these boards:
- Synced is green with a dot (MacRow and AndroidRow with tone success). Today the status line has no color (SyncStatusLine.swift:44). bae change.
- S3 rows read Provider, Endpoint, Region, Bucket. Today both show Bucket, Region, Endpoint (CloudProviderConnectedSection.swift:15-19, SettingsSyncSection.kt:174-176). bae change.

row-set-subsonic-note.text:
What the code needs for these boards (SubsonicSettingsTab.swift):
- The switch is what the person wants; the row's second line is what is happening, live from core as it changes (no Refresh): off, “Stream your library using a Subsonic app”; running, “Running”; on but not running, “Not running”, with why shown where it's fixed. The switch never springs back: core keeps it on and starts the server the moment nothing stands in the way.
- No Save buttons. Port, Username and Password save on Return or on leaving the field (CommittedTextField), each on its own; the pop-up on choosing. A port or network change restarts the server, and the new address under Available on is the confirmation (no “Restarting…” step). A username or password change applies to the next sign-in without a restart. A saved password shows as dots in the placeholder colour, since the app can't read it back; typing replaces it; no “Password saved” line.
- Why it isn't running, where it's fixed: no username or no password marks that row (field red, row's second line “Required to start the server”, danger); today the server runs with no password and nobody can sign in, and a missing username is refused with a notice. A port another app holds marks Port: “Another app is using this port”; one out of range, “Use a number from 1 to 65535”. Port is MacPortField: five digits wide, digits only. The chosen network gone: the line reads “Not running: Wi-Fi isn’t connected”, no notice. Any other start failure: a danger notice under the switch, “Subsonic server could not start”, with Details.
- “Available on” is a pop-up in place of the “Allow connections from other devices on your network” switch: This Mac only (127.0.0.1, the default), then each network interface that has an address, by the name System Settings gives its service (else the interface's own name, else its BSD name, such as “utun4”), with its IPv4 address (“Wi-Fi · 192.168.1.20”, “Tailscale · 100.64.0.3”), then Every network (0.0.0.0). The choice is stored as the interface (its BSD name, en0), not its address: a new address on it moves the server to that address. While it runs, the address an app connects to is the Available on row's second line, “Apps connect at http://<its address>:<port>” on one network, http://localhost:<port> on This Mac only; with more than one address (Every network), “Apps connect at:” and a bullet per address followed by its interface's name: “• http://192.168.1.20:4533 (Wi-Fi)”, “• http://100.64.0.3:4533 (Tailscale)”. Not running, no address. Never 0.0.0.0, and no /rest. Each address is MacCopyText: selectable, with a copy button after it while the pointer is over it. Core lists the interfaces and binds; the app names them. The menu lists only interfaces that have an address, except the chosen one: while it has none it stays, ticked, as “Wi-Fi · not connected”, and it drops out once another is chosen. Core watches address changes (the if-watch crate: macOS's network configuration notifications, Linux netlink, Windows' address-change notifications; it reports addresses only, so on each change core re-reads the interfaces with if-addrs, already in the build through mdns-sd) and moves, stops or starts the server as the chosen interface's IPv4 address comes, changes or goes. Today it binds once at start and never notices.
- Username and Password sit together in a “Sign-in” box, with the note “Subsonic apps sign in with this username and password. The password is kept in this Mac’s keychain.”
- On but not running, for any reason, it shows outside Settings too: the sidebar's Subsonic carries an “Offline” chip, as Library's does (warning; danger when it could not start), and the Activity panel's Needs Attention lists “Subsonic server isn’t running” (same tone) with “Open Subsonic Settings”, which closes the panel and opens this pane, and an × that takes it out of the panel without fixing it; it comes back if the server stops again after running. Clicking the row opens the alert with why and the causes. The toolbar's Activity button carries its warning mark while the row is listed. Off is a choice: no chip, no row.
Every locale.

sync-rules.text:
How the sync states behave:
- coven gives the state; bae picks the words and the fix.
- When several hold, the first shows: Not synced, Removed from the library, Device needs reset, Update needed, Signed out, No access, Folder missing, Clock is wrong, Cloud full, Offline · unsent changes, Offline, Sync failed, Syncing…, Waiting to sync, Synced.
- Not synced is desktop only: a phone joins a library and never makes one.
- Syncing… only while something is sent or received, not on quiet passes.
- Waiting to sync: online, with changes held back. Gray when uploads are paused or an upload waits to retry; amber when the provider asked bae to wait, saying when it resumes. Android never uploads files, so its only reason is the provider's wait.
- Synced means data and files both: a file still uploading is Syncing….
- Offline with changes waiting is Offline · unsent changes, with no count.
- Signed out names the provider and its sign-in: Dropbox and OneDrive sign in from bae; iCloud from System Settings. S3 has no sign-in: it reads Access key not accepted and asks for a new key for the same bucket. An expired sign-in reads the same as none saved.
- Sync failed: any failure with no state of its own, its cause in plain words, always with Retry now; it also retries by itself. A file that can't be uploaded (missing, or changed since import) names the file until it's back as it was; nothing skips it. Phones never upload, so their causes are local ones, a provider error or a damaged change.
- The Library page's Sync row shows the state only. The top of the Sync page shows the state, its cause and its fix, then Last synced under a problem state (never under Synced), then the storage details.
- Settings' Library row (Android) and the settings sidebar's Library item (macOS) show the state only when it's amber or red.
- No Sync stopped, no Checking sync… and no Disconnect anywhere.
- No raw ids on the Sync page: a row shows a name or isn't there.

no upload or download speed limits on any platform (CloudKit can't be paced). Android has no Pause uploads: a phone never uploads files. On macOS, while uploads or downloads are paused the sidebar shows an amber Paused beside Transfers, with ↑, ↓ or ⇅ for which.

- Closing the library…
- Leaving the library…
- Deleting this device’s files…
A library that has to open first, to count what it hasn’t sent, can show (core.library.open_step.*):

If the removal fails, the alert’s text is the error’s own line from core (core.error.category.*), such as “Couldn’t reach the cloud. Check your connection and try again.”

activity-progress.text:
How a transfer line counts (macOS and Android):
- The count is releases done of the batch: “1 of 3 releases”. A release counts as done once all its files are.
- The bar is bytes, not releases: the bytes done of the whole batch’s bytes. It moves while a release’s files transfer, even while the count stays put.
- Uploads count the bytes the provider confirmed (coven’s upload progress); pins and make-locals count the bytes downloaded and verified.
- A batch is everything the queue has held since it was last empty, so both the count’s total and the bar’s total only grow, and start over once the queue empties.
- Syncing changes has no count, so its bar moves.

set-import-discogs-tip.text:
The ⓘ after Search MusicBrainz opens the lower popover: “MusicBrainz” is a link to musicbrainz.org; it needs no account or key, but not everyone knows what it is. The ⓘ after Search Discogs opens the upper one. “Discogs” and “get your free API key” are links, in the accent. The key is kept in this Mac’s keychain, in an entry that stays on this device (coven’s host secret).

Search Discogs works like any switch: it's always usable. Off, the key field under it is greyed; on, the field takes a key and Save checks it. Turning it off with a saved key asks first (“Turn off Discogs?” / “Your saved key will be cleared.”, Turn Off and Cancel), then clears the key. A working key shows “Key saved” as the row’s second line, in secondary text, and no Remove: turning the switch off is how a key goes. Today the switch is greyed until a key validates (ImportSettingsTab.swift:108, `.disabled(!setting.canChange)`).

code-set-formats.text:
What the code needs for these boards:
- The Formats pane is “Save as”, in the sidebar and its title (SettingsView.swift, `.formats`); its list keeps the heading “Formats”, and the note “Formats appear in Save as… on tracks and releases.” goes.
- Each format row ends in a ⋯ button (MoreMenu) with Edit… and Delete…, in place of the Track and Release toggles and the minus (PresetRow, FormatsSettingsTab.swift). Clicking the row still opens the editor. Delete… asks as the minus does today.
- A format keeps its Name, first in the editor, prefilled when added with the format's name and the next free number: “FLAC”, then “FLAC (2)”, “FLAC (3)”; while it is still that prefill, changing Format re-prefills it. Rows show only the name, no grey line; the save panel's Format pop-up lists the names, then a separator and Edit Formats…, which opens Settings at the Save as pane in front of the save panel; the panel's pop-up follows any change made there, and a format added there is chosen in it. Names are unique on every add and edit: a taken name turns the Name field red with “Another format is named “MP3”.” and Done off, and core refuses one; “(2)” is only the prefill. Two formats may save the same way. Names stay stored, not made from the settings: encoder settings to come will be more than a name can say.
- “Add format…” is a button under the list, on the right, as Add library… is on Welcome; today “+ Add format” sits inside the box.
- No Defaults section: Save as starts with the format last used for any save, track or release (one stored choice in place of default_track_save_preset and default_release_save_preset).
- Track and Release go from the codebase: every format shows in Save as for tracks and releases. Core drops a preset's applies-to-track and applies-to-release.
- The editor is Name, Format and its one quality setting, nothing else; Embed cover art moves to Extras, one setting for every format. Bit depth for FLAC, WAV and AIFF: “Same as source” (the default) or “16-bit”; core's SaveBitDepth becomes those two, so a CD stays 16-bit where a fixed 24 pads it today. Bitrate for MP3, AAC and Opus, a pop-up, not a text field.
- The Format pop-up lists lossless first, then a separator, then lossy: FLAC, WAV, AIFF / MP3, AAC, Opus (core's SaveFormat::ALL order today: FLAC, MP3, AAC, Opus, WAV, AIFF).
- Bitrates, from what each encoder does with bae's bit_rate (bae-audio/src/encode.rs sets bit_rate = kbps × 1000): MP3 is libmp3lame at a constant bitrate, which has only 14 legal values (32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 320) and rounds anything between, so its pop-up lists exactly those; AAC (FFmpeg's own encoder) 96, 128, 160, 192, 256, 320; Opus (libopus, max 510) 64, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256.
- No Advanced. Every save writes one file per track by one rule: a track's gap goes at the end of the track before, and hidden audio before track 1 stays at the start of track 1 (today's AppendToPreviousIncludingHtoa). An image + CUE source is split at its track marks. Core drops SavePregapPlacement and single file + CUE.
- A release save of a track already in the chosen format at the same depth copies its audio without re-encoding, writing tags, cover and name fresh.
- Names: one box on the pane, out of each format's editor, with two naming fields labeled above them. File name names each track's file in every format (one stored pattern in place of each preset's save_preset_filename_token). Folder name names the folder a release save makes. A pattern is text with values in it as chips, an NSTokenField as Finder's rename Format field is: the person types between chips, and Delete after a chip or Forward Delete (fn-Delete) before it takes the whole chip out; chips still drag to reorder and come from the Add line. Stored as ordered pieces, each a value or typed text (save_filename_token and save_folder_token rows); rendering fills each value and keeps the text as typed, no longer joining with spaces, and an empty value leaves its text. Defaults: file [Track №] [Title], with a typed space between; folder [Artist] - [Album]. Text is kept as typed: spaces are not collapsed or trimmed (sanitize_filename_stem collapses runs today). Typed text that can't make a name turns the field red, and the preview line, which now sits right under the field with the Add line below it, becomes the error: “A name can’t start with “.”.” (typed text first in the pattern starting with .), “A name can’t contain “/”.” (the first of \ : ? * " < > | / in typed text), “A name can’t be empty.” (no pieces). The pattern is stored as typed; while it is invalid, saves name by its default pattern, and the error says nothing about that. A value's own characters are still written as coven writes a name (Some/Weird:Title → Some／Weird：Title). Both patterns add Album year, the album's own year (album.year), beside Release year, the release's (shown_year: its own year, else the album's). Folder values: Artist, Album, Album year, Release year, Label, Catalog number; file values: Title, Artist, Album, Album year, Release year, Track №, Disc №, Track total.
- Extras, all on: Embed cover art (from each format), Cover image in the folder (a release save writes cover.jpg) and Loudness tags (ReplayGain track and album gain and peak from the loudness measured at import).
- Spec §4.6 lists Save as's cases: one track converted; a whole release converted; an exact copy is Export.
- Deleting the format last used makes the first remaining one the last used, in the same write; the only format left can't be deleted: its ⋯ menu shows Delete… off (e23d69e33).
bae change, every locale.

code-set-storage.text:
What the code needs for these boards:
- A Storage page on both: on macOS a Settings pane after Transfers (SettingsView.swift); on Android a row after Transfers in the Settings list (SettingsMenu.kt:56-83), its second line the total. bae change.
- Sizes on this device, from core; nothing measures them today. Pinned: the pinned entries of coven's file cache. Cache: its unpinned entries in every namespace (release files, covers, artist images, avatars), with the Mac's catalog image cache (.bae/libraries/<id>/cache/remote-images-v2). Library: store.db, inputs.db, coven's settings and key files and its files/ folder. From before the reset: coven's discarded-device-* folders. Read when the page opens and again as they change. coven change (its per-namespace total, file_cache.rs:328, is crate-private and doesn't split pinned from unpinned) and bae change.
- Clear Cache removes every unpinned entry and the catalog image cache in one go; pinned copies stay. Dimmed while the cache is empty. Nothing clears the cache today: evict_file is wrapped for tests only (bae-store coven_capabilities.rs:380). The old remote-images folder, left by 939b1aa76, goes. coven change and bae change.
- Keep up to: 1 GB, 5 GB, 10 GB, 20 GB (the default), 50 GB; the limit on cached release files, per device. Pinned copies don't count toward it: today a namespace's total adds its pinned entries (coven file_cache_schema.rs:39-44), so 20 GB pinned leaves no room to cache a played track. bae sets it with set_cache_budget, which it never calls; the 20 GiB is fixed in bae-records/src/synced.rs:21-25. coven change and bae change.
- Unpin removes the release's copies from this device at once, even with room in the cache. Today unpinning releases the pins and evicts the namespace only down to its budget (coven.md, Unpinning), so the copies stay as cache. coven change.
- Ask before unpinning, on by default, per device: while on, Unpin asks first (the Unpin boards on the Library page), and Don't show this again there turns it off. Mac: .dialogSuppressionToggle on the alert. bae change.
- From before the reset: shown only while a discarded-device folder exists, which today stays forever (coven device_reset.rs:24, 125-128). Delete… asks, then removes it. coven change (a call that deletes it) and bae change.
- Local releases' originals stay in the person's folders and aren't counted.
Every locale.
